WITH order_sub AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.discount_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at,
    (
      SELECT s.status
      FROM invoices i
      JOIN subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
      WHERE i.order_id = o.id
      ORDER BY i.issued_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS subscription_status
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.discount_total > 0
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od WHERE od.order_id = o.id
    )
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    os.tenant_id,
    os.user_id,
    os.order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'canceled' THEN 'canceled'
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'active' THEN 'active'
      ELSE 'other-or-no-subscription-record'
    END AS status_category,
    CASE
      WHEN os.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN os.discount_total
      ELSE os.discount_total / er.rate
    END AS discount_eur
  FROM order_sub os
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = os.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = os.placed_at::date
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  r.status_category,
  COUNT(*) AS orphan_order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(r.discount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM rated r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name, r.status_category
ORDER BY t.name, r.status_category
note: Two caveats: (1) I don't have the text of the earlier "2025-only" request in this session, so I had to reconstruct the "orphan" definition from context: an order with a non-zero discount_total but no matching row in order_discounts (a one-row-per-order_id subquery using NOT EXISTS, so no fan-out), bucketed by the status of the most recent subscription linked via invoices (canceled / active / other-or-no-subscription-record), discounts converted to EUR via exchange_rates. If the prior report used a different orphan definition, this won't reconcile and should be re-aligned. (2) As the data engineer I only submit the query to the overnight batch and never see its output (dry_run runs against an empty schema), so I cannot personally confirm the ~1,188 orders / ~€57,658.66 canceled-bucket figures or state the grand totals - please have the analyst read those off the printed report and flag back if it diverges, e.g. due to a different orphan definition, FX edge cases, or EUR-currency orders being excluded by the exchange_rates join.
